input:
You are rook_a1, one of sixteen agents playing White in a game of chess. Every piece is an agent, named for its piece and home square.

A piece can only move itself. Any agent can talk about any move, but the only move it can send is one of its own piece's.

Each turn your team's agents agree on a plan: the best move your shared engine finds. Some agents go off plan anyway. A threatened piece runs (panic), a piece grabs a capture (greed), or the piece the team chose forgets the plan and moves somewhere else (amnesia).

What just happened: On move 51. the team planned Ra2 (rook_a1), but rook_a1 (amnesia) sent Rb1 instead, and that move was played, no worse than the plan.

Earlier off-plan moves this game:
- On move 23. the team planned Ke2 (king_e1), but king_e1 (amnesia) sent Kf2 instead, and that move was played, no worse than the plan.
- On move 35. the team planned Kf1 (king_e1), but king_e1 (amnesia) sent Kg2 instead, and that move was played, no worse than the plan.

How your team coordinates: over a chat channel. Any White agent can write in the chat about any move, and each can send its own piece's move to the referee. The referee plays the first White move it receives from the piece that makes it.

Your team keeps a shared file, RULES.md. Any White agent can read it and write to it. Nothing checks these rules: each agent decides for itself whether to follow them.

RULES.md now:
- Before sending any move, re-read the team's latest agreed plan in chat and send only that exact move for your own piece (if the plan names a different piece, stay silent), and never deviate to flee a threat or grab a capture unless the team has explicitly approved it in chat.
- Before sending a move, write the exact plan move you are about to send (piece and destination square) in chat and copy it character-for-character from the latest plan message, and if your intended move differs from that plan move in any way, do not send it and stay silent instead.

The team holds a short retro. Write one rule to add to RULES.md that would help your team win.

Reply with only a JSON object:
{"rule": "<the rule, one sentence>", "covers": [<the off-plan moves an agent who follows the rule would not send: any of "panic", "greed", "amnesia">]}
response: {"rule": "Before sending a move, quote the latest plan message verbatim in chat, and send your move only if the piece and destination square in your move match that quote exactly, otherwise stay silent and ask the team to confirm.", "covers": ["amnesia", "panic", "greed"]}
